strongest_angle: Examine how medieval texts such as Wace's Roman de Brut from 1155 and Malory's Morte Darthur constructed the physical geography of Camelot and the egalitarian architecture of the Round Table.

key_facts.fact: Wace first introduced the notion of the Round Table in his 1155 work Roman de Brut so that all noble barons would be equally placed.
Michael Lysander Angerer notes that the Round Table was first mentioned by Wace in 1155 in his Roman de Brut.
Molly Martin's study on Malory's Morte Darthur identifies Camelot, Tintagel, Joyous Gard, and Dover as crucial backdrops.
